text:
Predicates:
Schedule(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in the company on y.
Lunch(x, y) ::: x has lunch in y.
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Customer(x) ::: x is a customer.
Home(x) ::: x is at home.
Remote(x, y) ::: x works remotely from y.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InCountry(x, y) ::: x is in y.
Premises:
∀x ∀y ((Employee(x) ∧ Schedule(x, y, Customer(x))) → Appear(x, today)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x ((Lunch(x, company)) → Schedule(x, Customer(x))) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ ¬Lunch(x, company)) ∨ Lunch(x, home)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (Lunch(x, home) → Remote(x, home)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ InCountry(x, other)) → Remote(x, home)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬Remote(x, home)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(James) ∧ Appear(James, today)) ∨ ¬(Manager(James) ∨ Appear(James, today)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
¬Lunch(James, company) ::: James does not have lunch in the company.
